description.narrative:
The Endowment Fund (EF) is intended to secure the essential operations of gene banks to safeguard their genetic material. The prioritization among the many gene banks is divided into three categories/levels. Levels 1 and 2 comprise international gene banks operating under Article 15 of the FAO Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources, while Level 3 includes other important national and private genetic collections.
The annual withdrawal from the EF is limited to a maximum of 4% of the fund's total value. To ensure the conservation of all diversity in gene banks, Crop Trust has estimated that the cost will amount to approximately USD 34 million—this would secure all genetic material in the Article 15 gene banks (19 gene banks, including CGIAR gene banks), as well as the most significant national and private collections. This corresponds to a capital fund of USD 850 million, whereas the current fund stands at USD 253 million.
To support the CGIAR gene banks and operate the secretariat, the EF needs to reach USD 500 million. Between 2005 and 2022, the EF has contributed over USD 74 million to support Crop Trust’s mission. As of December 31st, 2024, the fund's value is USD 357 million - the total capital contributions since its inception, amounts to USD 297 million.
Germany is the EF’s largest donor, with a total contribution of USD 83,2 million, representing just under 28% of the total contributions to the fund. The United States is the second-largest donor, with a total contribution of USD 81,5 million. Norway is the third-largest donor, having contributed a total of USD 33.7 million—the most recent contribution from Norway was NOK 25 million in 2024.
